extraction.Name: Eddie Cuny
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent in fee to his 160 acre allotment, when it was issued, April 13,1918, but the Indian Agency told him that, if he did not accept it, and pay his taxes, it would be taxed any way, and finally sold for the taxes, so he accepted the patent
extraction.Buyer: Isaac H. Chase, of Rapid City, South Dakota, who foreclosed on his allotment in 1920
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: when the mortgage became due, he was unable to meet the obligation, and that Mr. Chase foreclosed on his allotment; he considers he received a very poor price for his land; and that, personally, he never paid any taxes on this allotment
extraction.Occupation/Income: carries mail for the United States Government for his living; receives $175.00 per year lease money on his wife's and children's land
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, health good; has a wife and seven children to support; all of the family have good health; borrowed $800.00 from Isaac H. Chase in 1919 to purchase horses, giving Chase a mortgage on his allotment; did not sell his place for any debts incurred prior to receiving his patent in fee; has never received any help from the County, State, nor the United States Government; document sworn March 12, 1929 | ORIGINAL_TRIBE_VALUE: "Shannon County, South Dakota (Pine Ridge area)" (normalized 2026-04-28 to canonical 'Pine Ridge')
